facts.statement: Fossils of Olorotitan were discovered in the Udurchukan Formation near the Amur River in Eastern Russia.
facts.quote: The remains were found in the Udurchukan Formation beds of Kundur, Arkharinsky District, Amur Oblast, Eastern Russia, in the vicinity of the Amur River.

facts.statement: Pascal Godefroit and colleagues formally described and named the species in 2003.
facts.quote: Pascal Godefroit and colleagues described and named it as a new species in 2003.

facts.statement: This specimen was the first nearly complete dinosaur skeleton described from Russia.
facts.quote: It was the first nearly complete dinosaur specimen to be described from Russia

facts.statement: It holds the record for the most complete lambeosaurine skeleton found outside of western North America.
facts.quote: It was the first nearly complete dinosaur specimen to be described from Russia, and is the most complete lambeosaurine skeleton discovered anywhere outside of western North America.

facts.statement: The genus name means "titanic swan" due to its exceptionally long neck compared to other hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: The generic name Olorotitan means "titanic swan" because its neck is longer when compared with other hadrosaurs

facts.statement: The species name arharensis refers to Arhara County, the location where the fossil was found.
facts.quote: while the specific descriptor arharensis refers to Arhara County where the fossil was found.

facts.statement: Olorotitan was a large hadrosaurid reaching up to 8 meters in length, 3.5 meters in height, and weighing between 2.6 and 3.4 metric tons.
facts.quote: It was a large hadrosaurid, comparable with other large lambeosaurines such as Parasaurolophus cyrtocristatus, and may have grown up to 8 m in length, up to 3.5 m in height and within the range of 2.6 - 3.4 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: The animal is characterized by a large, flaring hollow crest that is distinct from those of its North American relatives.
facts.quote: It is characterized by the large flaring hollow crest adorning its skull, very distinct from the crests of all of its North American relatives.

facts.statement: Its neck was exceptionally elongated, possessing eighteen vertebrae, which exceeded the previous known maximum of fifteen for hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: The skull itself was supported by a rather elongated neck, having eighteen vertebrae, exceeding the previous hadrosaurid maximum of fifteen.

facts.statement: The proximal third of the tail featured articulations between neural spine tips that made that section particularly rigid.
facts.quote: Further along the vertebral series, in the proximal third of the tail, there are articulations between the tips of the neural spines, making that caudal area particularly rigid

facts.statement: Some sources suggest the animal may have reached lengths of 11 to 12 meters.
facts.quote: pudiendo haber alcanzado los 11 y 12 metros de largo.

facts.statement: The crest consisted of a bone plate between the skull and neck, identified as highly developed nasal bones forming a hatchet or fan shape.
facts.quote: La cresta consistía en una placa ósea situada entre la región dorsocaudal del cráneo y el cuello, que se identificó como unos huesos nasales muy desarrollados, que le daba a la misma una forma de hacha o abanico.

facts.statement: To support this structure, Olorotitan possessed eighteen cervical vertebrae instead of the typical fifteen.
facts.quote: Para sostener esta estructura, Olorotitan poseía un número mayor de vértebras cervicales, 18 en lugar de 15.

facts.statement: Its sacrum contained 15 or 16 vertebrae, which was at least three more than other hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: El sacro, con 15 o 16 vértebras, tenía por lo menos 3 piezas más que la de ototros hadrosáuridos.

facts.statement: The proximal third of the tail had fused caudal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Un 1/3 proximal de la cola tenía las vértebras caudales fusionadas.

facts.statement: The skull was long and massive.
facts.quote: Olorotitan tiene un cráneo largo y masivo.

facts.statement: It is distinguished by a strange hollow comb on its head, a feature unique among North American hadrosaurs.
facts.quote: Se distingue por un extraño peine hueco en la cabeza. Ninguno de los hadrosaurios del continente norteamericano tiene una igual.

facts.statement: The zygomatic bone was 0.9 meters long, featuring a very high alveolar crest and an extremely straight anterior margin.
facts.quote: El hueso cigomático, con un arco más corto que otros lambeosaurinos y un margen anterior extremadamente recto, lleva una cresta alveolar muy alta. Su longitud es de 0,9 metros

facts.statement: Its bony teeth were lower than those of Charonosaurus.
facts.quote: Los dientes óseos son más bajos que los de Charonosaurus.

facts.statement: It was a bipedal or quadrupedal herbivore with a sophisticated skull allowing a grinding motion and hundreds of continually replaced teeth.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaurid, Olorotitan would have been a bipedal/quadrupedal herbivore, eating plants with a sophisticated skull that permitted a grinding motion analogous to chewing, and was furnished with hundreds of continually-replaced teeth.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest its tall, broad hollow crest likely functioned in identification by sight and sound.
facts.quote: Its tall, broad hollow crest, formed out of expanded skull bones containing the nasal passages, probably functioned in identification by sight and sound.

facts.statement: It lived approximately 72 to 66 million years ago in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 72 a 66 millones de años, durante el Maastrichtiense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places it closest to Corythosaurus and Hypacrosaurus.
facts.quote: Godefroit and his coauthors found through a phylogenetic analysis that it was closest to Corythosaurus and Hypacrosaurus.

facts.statement: It belongs to the tribe Corythosaurini.
facts.quote: tribus: Corythosaurini

facts.statement: The diversity of Asian lambeosaurines at the end of the Mesozoic suggests climatic or ecological differences compared to North America.
facts.quote: Unlike the situation in North America, where lambeosaurines are virtually absent from Late Maastrichtian rocks, Asian lambeosaurines are diverse and common at the end of the Mesozoic, suggesting climatic or ecological differences.

facts.statement: It is currently unknown what specific function the crest served.
facts.quote: Lo que se desconoce es la función que desempeñaba.

facts.statement: The tail of Olorotitan was long and constructed from at least 70 vertebrae.
facts.quote: La cola era larga, construida por al menos 70 vértebras.

facts.statement: Olorotitan possessed a shoulder blade that was longer than that of other members of its family.
facts.quote: Olorotitan tenía un omóplato más alargado que otros representantes de su familia.

facts.statement: The femur of Olorotitan did not differ in size from the tibia.
facts.quote: El fémur no difiere en tamaño de la tibia.

facts.statement: The genus name Olorotitan translates to "giant swan," and the species name arharensis refers to the Arhara district where it was found.
facts.quote: El nombre del género se traduce como "cisne gigante", mientras que el nombre de la especie hace referencia a la localidad donde fuera encontrado, el condado de Arhara.

facts.statement: Olorotitan is distinguished from other crested duck-billed dinosaurs by an unusual crest that takes the shape of an axe or sail at its distal end.
facts.quote: Olorotitan se diferencia de otros dinosaurios de picos de pato crestados por la posición de una inusual cresta que en su extremo distal toma una forma de hacha o vela.

facts.statement: The remains of Olorotitan, unearthed between 1999 and 2001, represent the most complete dinosaur find in the Russian Federation and the most complete Lambeosaurinae skeleton found outside North America.
facts.quote: los restos de Olorotitan, desenterrados entre 1999-2001, son el hallazgo de dinosaurios más completo en la Federación de Rusia, así como el esqueleto de Lambeosaurinae más completo fuera de Norteamérica.

facts.statement: Olorotitan was described by Pascal Godefroit and colleagues in mid-2003.
facts.quote: Fue descrito por Pascal Godefroit y colaboradores a mediados de 2003.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Olorotitan was discovered in the Tsagayan Formation in the Amur region of eastern Russia.
facts.quote: El espécimen fue descubierto en la Formación Tsagayan, en la región de Amur, en el extremo oriental de Rusia.

facts.statement: Like all hadrosaurids, Olorotitan was a bipedal/quadrupedal herbivore that ate plants using a sophisticated skull capable of mastication-like movement, powered by batteries of hundreds of replacement teeth.
facts.quote: Como todo hadrosáurido, Olorotitan fue un bípedo/cuadrúpedo herbívoro, comiendo plantas con un sofisticado cráneo que le permitía un movimiento análogo a la masticación, con baterías de cientos de dientes que remplazaban a los que se usaban a medida que se gastaban.

facts.statement: The high, hollow crest of Olorotitan's skull contained air channels connected to the respiratory tract, likely functioning for both visual and acoustic signaling.
facts.quote: La alta y hueca cresta formada por la expansión de los huesos del cráneo estaba surcada por canales aéreos conectados a las vías respiratorias, probablemente funcionaran como un medio de reconocimiento tanto visual como sonoro.

facts.statement: Olorotitan lived during the Maastrichtian stage, approximately 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Maastrichtian to Maastrichtian (72.2 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Olorotitan belongs to the subfamily Lambeosaurinae within the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Lambeosaurinae

facts.statement: Olorotitan is classified in the dinosaur family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Olorotitan is a member of the dinosaur order Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
